lines.text: The arm's setters are private, so nothing outside the arm can call them. A command is the only way in.
Here's the first one. It pushes at three volts.
You've seen the arrow before. It hands the job over, and this part runs that job every loop, for as long as the command runs.
The name on the end is what makes it a command. Leave it off, and the build fails with an error that doesn't tell you why.
The other two work the same way: six volts, and stop. Even stop sends its zero every loop.
Try it. Pick a command and watch the request it sends, then pick another.
Look at the word at the end of every name. Hold. None of these ever finishes. Each one runs until something else takes the arm.
So what takes it? On the robot, it's the driver's thumb, and that's the next lesson.
